## SALESFORCE_LIST_OPPORTUNITIES
Lists opportunities from Salesforce using SOQL query, allowing flexible filtering, sorting, and field selection. Results are paginated up to ~2000 rows per batch; check `done`, `totalSize`, and `nextRecordsUrl` fields to detect and retrieve additional pages, or use a SOQL `LIMIT` clause to cap results. For complex queries rejected by this tool, use `SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY` instead.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListOpportunitiesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "default": "SELECT Id, Name, StageName, CloseDate, Amount, Probability, Type, LeadSource, AccountId FROM Opportunity",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT Id, Name, Amount FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won'",
        "SELECT Id, Name, CloseDate FROM Opportunity ORDER BY CloseDate DESC LIMIT 10",
        "SELECT Id, Name, Amount FROM Opportunity WHERE Amount > 50000 AND CloseDate = THIS_QUARTER",
        "SELECT Id, Name, Owner.Name, Owner.Email FROM Opportunity"
      ],
      "description": "SOQL query to fetch opportunities. Use standard SOQL syntax to filter, sort, and limit results.  Omitting a `WHERE` clause returns all opportunities including historical ones. Results have no default sort order; include `ORDER BY CloseDate DESC` to retrieve recent opportunities first.IMPORTANT: Only use standard Salesforce fields unless you have confirmed that custom fields exist in the target org. Custom fields (ending with '__c') are org-specific and may not exist in all Salesforce instances. For relationship queries (e.g., Owner.Name), only use standard fields on the related object. To discover available fields, use the SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT action first.",
      "human_parameter_name": "SOQL Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Type the SOQL query that defines which opportunities to retrieve and which fields to return. Use it to filter, sort, and limit results so you get exactly the records you need. Note: Custom fields (ending with __c) must exist in your Salesforce org."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_LIST_PRICEBOOK_ENTRIES
Lists pricebook entries from Salesforce using SOQL query, allowing flexible filtering, sorting, and field selection. Use this to map product names to pricebook entry IDs needed for opportunity line items. When using returned IDs with SALESFORCE_ADD_OPPORTUNITY_LINE_ITEM, always filter with WHERE IsActive = true — inactive entries cause REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING or INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY errors.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListPricebookEntriesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "default": "SELECT Id, Name, Product2Id, Pricebook2Id, UnitPrice, IsActive, ProductCode, Product2.Name FROM PricebookEntry",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT Id, Name, Product2.Name, UnitPrice FROM PricebookEntry WHERE IsActive = true",
        "SELECT Id, Product2.Name, Pricebook2Id, UnitPrice FROM PricebookEntry WHERE Pricebook2Id = '01sXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'",
        "SELECT Id, ProductCode, Product2.Name, UnitPrice FROM PricebookEntry WHERE Product2.Name LIKE '%Widget%' ORDER BY UnitPrice DESC"
      ],
      "description": "SOQL query to fetch pricebook entries. Use standard SOQL syntax to filter, sort, and limit results.",
      "human_parameter_name": "SOQL Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Type the SOQL query that defines which pricebook entries to retrieve and which fields to return. Use it to filter by product name, pricebook, or price to find the exact entry you need."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_LIST_PRICEBOOKS
Lists pricebooks from Salesforce using SOQL query, allowing flexible filtering, sorting, and field selection. Use this to map pricebook names to IDs.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListPricebooksRequest",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "default": "SELECT Id, Name, IsActive, IsStandard, Description FROM Pricebook2",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT Id, Name, IsActive FROM Pricebook2 WHERE IsActive = true",
        "SELECT Id, Name, IsStandard FROM Pricebook2 ORDER BY Name ASC",
        "SELECT Id, Name, Description FROM Pricebook2 WHERE IsStandard = false LIMIT 10"
      ],
      "description": "SOQL query to fetch pricebooks. Use standard SOQL syntax to filter, sort, and limit results.",
      "human_parameter_name": "SOQL Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Type the SOQL query that defines which pricebooks to retrieve and which fields to return. Use it to filter, sort, and limit results so you get exactly the records you need."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_LOG_CALL
Logs a completed phone call as a task in Salesforce with call-specific details like duration, type, and disposition.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "LogCallRequest",
  "properties": {
    "who_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Who Id",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "003XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
        "00QXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "ID of the Contact or Lead associated with the call. Invalid or non-existent IDs create orphaned or mislinked activity records.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Who ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The person you spoke with. Paste the Salesforce Contact or Lead ID to link the call to their record for easy tracking."
    },
    "subject": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject",
      "default": "Call",
      "examples": [
        "Call",
        "Follow-up Call",
        "Sales Call",
        "Support Call"
      ],
      "description": "Subject line for the call log. Defaults to 'Call'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Subject",
      "human_parameter_description": "A short title for the call log. Keep it descriptive so it\u2019s easy to recognize on timelines and reports."
    },
    "what_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "What Id",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "001XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
        "006XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
        "500XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "ID of the related record (Account, Opportunity, Case, etc.) associated with the call.",
      "human_parameter_name": "What ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The record this call is about (like an Account, Opportunity, or Case). Paste its Salesforce ID to attach the call to that record."
    },
    "comments": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Comments",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "Discussed product features and pricing. Customer interested in premium plan.",
        "Left voicemail about upcoming renewal.",
        "Resolved technical issue with login. Customer satisfied."
      ],
      "description": "Detailed notes or description of what was discussed during the call.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Comments",
      "human_parameter_description": "Notes about what was discussed and any next steps. Include enough detail so teammates understand the context."
    },
    "call_date": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Call Date",
      "examples": [
        "2025-08-28",
        "2025-09-01"
      ],
      "description": "Date of the call in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today if not specified.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Call Date",
      "human_parameter_description": "The date the call happened (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave blank to use today\u2019s date automatically."
    },
    "call_type": {
      "enum": [
        "Inbound",
        "Outbound",
        "Internal"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "CallTypeEnum",
      "default": "Outbound",
      "description": "Standard Salesforce Task CallType values. This is a restricted picklist.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Call Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "How the call happened\u2014Inbound, Outbound, or Internal. This is a restricted field that only accepts these three standard values."
    },
    "custom_fields": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Custom Fields",
      "examples": [
        {
          "Call_Outcome__c": "Left Voicemail",
          "Follow_Up_Required__c": true
        },
        {
          "External_Call_ID__c": "CALL-12345"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names typically end with '__c' (e.g., 'Call_Outcome__c').",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "anyOf": [
          {
            "type": "string"
          },
          {
            "type": "integer"
          },
          {
            "type": "number"
          },
          {
            "type": "boolean"
          },
          {
            "type": "null"
          }
        ]
      },
      "human_parameter_name": "Custom Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide custom Salesforce fields to store org-specific call data. Use the API field name (ending in '__c') as the key."
    },
    "call_disposition": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Call Disposition",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "Contact Made",
        "Left Message",
        "No Answer",
        "Busy",
        "Wrong Number",
        "Successful"
      ],
      "description": "Outcome or result of the call. Restricted picklist \u2014 only org-configured values are accepted; unlisted values cause validation errors.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Call Disposition",
      "human_parameter_description": "What happened on the call. Use a clear outcome like 'Contact Made' or 'Left Message' to summarize the result."
    },
    "call_duration_seconds": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Call Duration Seconds",
      "examples": [
        300,
        600,
        1800
      ],
      "description": "Duration of the call in seconds.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Call Duration",
      "human_parameter_description": "How long the call lasted, in seconds. This helps measure talk time and reporting."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_LOG_EMAIL_ACTIVITY
Creates an EmailMessage record to log email activity in Salesforce, associating it with related records. Requires EmailMessage insert permissions enabled at the org level; some orgs block this entirely.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "LogEmailActivityRequest",
  "required": [
    "subject",
    "from_address",
    "to_address",
    "related_to_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Status",
      "default": "3",
      "examples": [
        "0",
        "3",
        "5"
      ],
      "description": "Status of the email. 0=New, 1=Read, 2=Replied, 3=Sent, 4=Forwarded, 5=Draft",
      "human_parameter_name": "Status",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose how this email should be marked in Salesforce (for example, New, Sent, or Draft). If unsure, keep the default."
    },
    "subject": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject",
      "examples": [
        "Follow-up on our meeting",
        "Product information requested",
        "Contract renewal discussion"
      ],
      "description": "Subject line of the email.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Subject",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the email\u2019s subject line so the message is easy to recognize and find later."
    },
    "html_body": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Html Body",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "<html><body><p>Thank you for your time today.</p></body></html>",
        "<h1>Product Information</h1><p>Please see the details below...</p>"
      ],
      "description": "HTML body of the email. If provided, takes precedence over text_body for display.",
      "human_parameter_name": "HTML Body",
      "human_parameter_description": "Paste the formatted (HTML) version of the email content for rich formatting. If provided, this will be shown instead of the plain text."
    },
    "parent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent Id",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "500XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "ID of the parent record, typically a Case for case-related emails.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Parent ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the parent record ID if this email belongs under a specific parent (often a Case) to keep related messages organized."
    },
    "text_body": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Text Body",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "Thank you for your time today. Please find the attached proposal.",
        "As discussed, here are the product specifications you requested."
      ],
      "description": "Plain text body of the email.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Text Body",
      "human_parameter_description": "Paste the email content in plain text. Use this if you don\u2019t need rich formatting."
    },
    "cc_address": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Cc Address",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "manager@company.com",
        "team@company.com,support@company.com"
      ],
      "description": "CC email addresses (comma-separated if multiple).",
      "human_parameter_name": "CC Address",
      "human_parameter_description": "Add anyone you want to copy on the email. Separate multiple addresses with commas."
    },
    "to_address": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "To Address",
      "examples": [
        "customer@example.com",
        "jane@company.com,bob@company.com"
      ],
      "description": "Email addresses of the recipients (comma-separated if multiple).",
      "human_parameter_name": "To Address",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter one or more recipient email addresses. Separate multiple addresses with commas."
    },
    "bcc_address": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Bcc Address",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "archive@company.com",
        "compliance@company.com"
      ],
      "description": "BCC email addresses (comma-separated if multiple).",
      "human_parameter_name": "BCC Address",
      "human_parameter_description": "Add hidden recipients who should receive the email without others seeing their addresses."
    },
    "is_incoming": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Is Incoming",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Whether this is an incoming email (true) or outgoing email (false).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Is Incoming",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select whether the email was received (incoming) or sent (outgoing) so the direction is recorded correctly."
    },
    "from_address": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "From Address",
      "examples": [
        "sales@company.com",
        "john.doe@company.com"
      ],
      "description": "Email address of the sender.",
      "human_parameter_name": "From Address",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address the message was sent from. Use the sender\u2019s mailbox."
    },
    "message_date": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Date",
      "examples": [
        "2025-08-28T14:30:00",
        "2025-08-28T09:15:00-05:00"
      ],
      "description": "Date/time the email was sent in ISO format. Defaults to current time if not provided. Must be an explicit ISO datetime string; relative expressions like 'yesterday' cause validation errors.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Message Date",
      "human_parameter_description": "When the email was sent. Leave this blank to use the current time, or provide the date and time if you want to set it explicitly."
    },
    "custom_fields": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Custom Fields",
      "examples": [
        {
          "Email_Category__c": "Follow-up",
          "Customer_Visible__c": true
        },
        {
          "External_Message_ID__c": "MSG-98765"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Dictionary of custom field API names and their values. Custom field names typically end with '__c' (e.g., 'Email_Category__c').",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "human_parameter_name": "Custom Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide custom Salesforce fields to capture org-specific email metadata. Use the API field name (ending in '__c') as the key."
    },
    "related_to_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Related To Id",
      "examples": [
        "001XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
        "006XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
        "500XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "ID of the record to associate this email with (Account, Opportunity, Case, etc.). Must reference a supported object type (Account, Opportunity, Case, Contact, Lead, etc.); unsupported object types cause validation errors or create standalone records invisible on timelines.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Related To ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Paste the Salesforce record ID (e.g., Account, Opportunity, or Case) that this email should be linked to, so it appears on the right record."
    },
    "is_client_managed": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Is Client Managed",
      "default": true,
      "description": "Whether the email is client-managed (not sent through Salesforce).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Client Managed",
      "human_parameter_description": "Turn this on if the email was handled outside Salesforce. It helps track emails sent from external mail clients."
    },
    "is_externally_visible": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Is Externally Visible",
      "default": true,
      "description": "Whether the email is visible in customer portals/communities.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Externally Visible",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose whether customers can see this email in portals or communities."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_MASS_TRANSFER_OWNERSHIP
Transfers ownership of multiple records to a new owner in a single operation using Salesforce's composite API for better performance. Operation has no rollback; all provided records are reassigned immediately.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "MassTransferOwnershipRequest",
  "required": [
    "object_type",
    "record_ids",
    "new_owner_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "record_ids": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Record Ids",
      "examples": [
        [
          "001XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
          "001YYYYYYYYYYYYYYY"
        ],
        [
          "003XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
          "003YYYYYYYYYYYYYYY",
          "003ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of record IDs to transfer ownership.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Record IDs",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the Salesforce IDs of the records you want to transfer. You can paste multiple IDs if you're moving several records at once."
    },
    "object_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Object Type",
      "examples": [
        "Account",
        "Contact",
        "Lead",
        "Opportunity",
        "Case"
      ],
      "description": "The Salesforce object type for the records to transfer (e.g., Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Object Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select the type of Salesforce record you're transferring (for example, Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity). This ensures we update ownership on the correct kind of records."

    "new_owner_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "New Owner Id",
      "examples": [
        "005XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID of the new owner to transfer records to.",
      "human_parameter_name": "New Owner ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the Salesforce User ID of the person who should become the new owner. All listed records will be assigned to this user."
    },
    "trigger_assignment_rules": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Trigger Assignment Rules",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Whether to trigger Salesforce assignment rules when transferring records. Applies mainly to Leads and Cases where assignment rules may reassign the record or send notifications.",

      "human_parameter_description": "Choose whether to activate Salesforce assignment rules during the transfer. This is relevant for Leads and Cases where assignment rules may apply additional logic or notifications."

}
```

## SALESFORCE_PARAMETERIZED_SEARCH
Tool to execute RESTful search using parameters instead of SOSL clause. Use when you need to search across Salesforce objects with simple GET requests (URL parameters) or complex POST requests (JSON body with advanced filtering). POST method supports DataCategories, networks, orderBy constraints, and per-object filtering.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ParameterizedSearchRequest",
  "required": [
    "q"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "q": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Q",
      "examples": [
        "Test",
        "John Doe",
        "test@example.com",
        "555-1234"
      ],
      "description": "The search string to search for across Salesforce objects. This is the primary search term."
    },
    "in": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "In",
      "examples": [
        "ALL",
        "NAME",
        "EMAIL",
        "PHONE",
        "SIDEBAR"
      ],
      "description": "Search scope specifying which fields to search. Valid values: ALL, NAME, EMAIL, PHONE, SIDEBAR. Defaults to ALL."
    },
    "where": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Where",
      "examples": [
        "Type='Customer'",
        "CreatedDate>2024-01-01"
      ],
      "description": "Global filter conditions for the search results. Use standard SOQL WHERE clause syntax (without the 'WHERE' keyword)."
    },
    "fields": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      ],
      "title": "Fields",
      "examples": [
        "Account.Name,Account.Id",
        [
          "Id",
          "Name"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "For GET: comma-separated string of fields in format 'Object.field1,Object.field2'. For POST: array of field names to return globally across all objects."
    },
    "method": {
      "enum": [
        "GET",
        "POST"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Method",
      "default": "GET",
      "description": "HTTP method to use. Use GET for simple searches with URL parameters, or POST for complex searches with JSON body including advanced filtering."
    },
    "sobjects": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "title": "SObjectFilter",
            "required": [
              "name"
            ],
            "properties": {
              "name": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Name",
                "examples": [
                  "Account",
                  "Contact",
                  "Lead",
                  "Opportunity"
                ],
                "description": "The Salesforce object name to search (e.g., 'Account', 'Contact', 'Lead')."
              },
              "where": {
                "anyOf": [
                  {
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  {
                    "type": "null"
                  }
                ],
                "title": "Where",
                "default": null,
                "examples": [
                  "Industry = 'Technology'",
                  "CreatedDate > 2024-01-01"
                ],
                "description": "SOQL WHERE clause for filtering results (without the 'WHERE' keyword). Use standard SOQL syntax."
              },
              "fields": {
                "anyOf": [
                  {
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  {
                    "type": "null"
                  }
                ],
                "title": "Fields",
                "default": null,
                "examples": [
                  [
                    "Id",
                    "Name"
                  ],
                  [
                    "Id",
                    "FirstName",
                    "LastName",
                    "Email"
                  ]
                ],
                "description": "Array of field names to return for this object. If not specified, default fields will be returned."
              }
            },
            "description": "Specification for an sObject to search with optional field filtering."
          }
        }
      ],
      "title": "Sobjects",
      "examples": [
        "Account,Contact",
        "Lead"
      ],
      "description": "For GET: comma-separated string of object names (e.g., 'Account,Contact'). For POST: array of SObjectFilter objects with name, fields, and where clauses."
    },
    "overallLimit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Overall Limit",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of results to return across all objects. Helps control result set size."
    },
    "spellCorrection": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Spell Correction",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Enable spell correction for search terms to find results even with misspelled queries."
    },
    "defaultSearchScope": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Default Search Scope",
      "examples": [
        "ALL",
        "NAME"
      ],
      "description": "Default search scope for the query when not explicitly specified."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request model for Salesforce Parameterized Search supporting both GET and POST methods."
}
```

## SALESFORCE_PATCH_COMPOSITE_SOBJECTS
Tool to upsert up to 200 records using external ID field matching. Use when you need to create or update multiple records efficiently in a single API call based on an external ID field.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PatchCompositeSobjectsRequest",
  "required": [
    "sobject_name",
    "external_id_field_name",
    "records"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "records": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "integer"
            },
            {
              "type": "number"
            },
            {
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            {
              "type": "object",
              "additionalProperties": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "title": "Records",
      "examples": [
        [
          {
            "Name": "Acme Corporation",
            "attributes": {
              "type": "Account"
            },
            "BillingCity": "San Francisco",
            "External_Account_ID__c": "EXT-12345"
          }
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Array of record objects to upsert. Maximum 200 records. Each record must include the 'attributes' object with the 'type' field, and the external ID field value for matching."
    },
    "all_or_none": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "All Or None",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        false,
        true
      ],
      "description": "Controls transaction behavior. If true, rolls back all changes if any record fails. If false (default), commits successful records even if others fail."
    },
    "sobject_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sobject Name",
      "examples": [
        "Account",
        "Contact",
        "Lead",
        "CustomObject__c"
      ],
      "description": "The API name of the Salesforce object (e.g., 'Account', 'Contact', 'CustomObject__c')."
    },
    "external_id_field_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "External Id Field Name",
      "examples": [
        "External_Account_ID__c",
        "Custom_External_ID__c",
        "Id"
      ],
      "description": "The API name of the external ID field to use for matching records (e.g., 'External_Account_ID__c', 'Id'). This field must be defined as an external ID field in Salesforce."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_POST_COMPOSITE_GRAPH
Tool to execute multiple related REST API requests in a single transactional call with up to 500 subrequests per graph. Use when you need to perform multiple Salesforce operations atomically where all operations must succeed or fail together. Supports referencing output from one request as input to subsequent requests using @{referenceId.fieldName} syntax.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PostCompositeGraphRequest",
  "required": [
    "graphs"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "graphs": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "CompositeGraph",
        "required": [
          "graphId",
          "compositeRequest"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "graphId": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Graph Id",
            "examples": [
              "graph1",
              "accountCreation",
              "orderProcessing"
            ],
            "description": "Unique identifier for this graph. Must begin with an alphanumeric character, be less than 40 characters long, not contain a period (.), and be unique within the composite graph operation."
          },
          "compositeRequest": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "object",
              "title": "CompositeSubRequest",
              "required": [
                "method",
                "url",
                "referenceId"
              ],
              "properties": {
                "url": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "title": "Url",
                  "examples": [
                    "/services/data/v61.0/sobjects/Account/",
                    "/services/data/v61.0/sobjects/Contact/"
                  ],
                  "description": "The Salesforce REST API endpoint path (relative to base URL). Example: '/services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/Account'."
                },
                "body": {
                  "type": "object",
                  "title": "Body",
                  "examples": [
                    {
                      "Name": "Test Account"
                    },
                    {
                      "LastName": "Doe",
                      "FirstName": "John"
                    }
                  ],
                  "description": "Request payload containing the data for POST/PATCH/PUT operations. Required for POST, PATCH, PUT methods; optional for GET, DELETE methods.",
                  "additionalProperties": {
                    "anyOf": [
                      {
                        "type": "string"
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "integer"
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "number"
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "boolean"
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "array",
                        "items": {}
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "object",
                        "additionalProperties": true
                      },
                      {
                        "type": "null"
                      }
                    ]
                  }
                },
                "method": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "title": "Method",
                  "examples": [
                    "POST",
                    "GET",
                    "PATCH",
                    "PUT",
                    "DELETE"
                  ],
                  "description": "HTTP method for the subrequest. Valid values: GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE."
                },
                "referenceId": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "title": "Reference Id",
                  "examples": [
                    "refAccount1",
                    "refContact1",
                    "refOpportunity1"
                  ],
                  "description": "Unique identifier used to reference the output of this request in subsequent requests using @{referenceId.fieldName} syntax. Must be unique within the graph."
                }
              },
              "description": "Represents a single subrequest within a composite graph."
            },
            "title": "Composite Request",
            "examples": [
              [
                {
                  "url": "/services/data/v61.0/sobjects/Account/",
                  "body": {
                    "Name": "Test Account"
                  },
                  "method": "POST",
                  "referenceId": "refAccount1"
                }
              ]
            ],
            "description": "Array of individual REST API requests within this graph. Maximum 500 subrequests per graph. All operations succeed or fail together (transactional). Output from one request can be referenced in subsequent requests using @{referenceId.fieldName} syntax."
          }
        },
        "description": "Represents a single graph with multiple related subrequests."
      },
      "title": "Graphs",
      "examples": [
        [
          {
            "graphId": "graph1",
            "compositeRequest": [
              {
                "url": "/services/data/v61.0/sobjects/Account/",
                "body": {
                  "Name": "Test Account from Composite Graph"
                },
                "method": "POST",
                "referenceId": "refAccount1"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Array of graph objects. Each graph can contain up to 500 subrequests and reach up to 15 levels of depth. All operations within a graph succeed or fail together. Subrequests in one graph cannot reference subrequests from another graph."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request model for executing multiple related REST API requests in a single transactional call."
}
```

```json
            "title": "GraphResult",
            "required": [
              "graphId",
              "graphResponse",
              "isSuccessful"
            ],
            "properties": {
              "graphId": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Graph Id",
                "description": "Echoes back the graphId from the request to identify which graph these results belong to."
              },
              "isSuccessful": {
                "type": "boolean",
                "title": "Is Successful",
                "description": "Indicates whether the entire graph operation succeeded. If false, all operations in the graph are rolled back."
              },
              "graphResponse": {
                "type": "object",
                "title": "Graph Response",
                "required": [
                  "compositeResponse"
                ],
                "properties": {
                  "compositeResponse": {
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "object",
                      "title": "CompositeSubResponse",
                      "required": [
                        "body",
                        "httpStatusCode",
                        "referenceId"
                      ],
                      "properties": {
                        "body": {
                          "anyOf": [
                            {
                              "type": "object",
                              "title": "CompositeSubResponseBody",
                              "properties": {
                                "id": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "title": "Id",
                                  "description": "The Salesforce record ID for successful POST operations."
                                },
                                "errors": {
                                  "type": "array",
                                  "items": {
                                    "type": "object",
                                    "additionalProperties": {
                                      "anyOf": [
                                        {
                                          "type": "string"
                                        },
                                        {
                                          "type": "array",
                                          "items": {
                                            "type": "string"
                                          }
                                        }
                                      ]
                                    }
                                  },
                                  "title": "Errors",
                                  "description": "Array of errors (empty if successful). Each error object contains statusCode, message, and fields."
                                },
                                "success": {
                                  "type": "boolean",
                                  "title": "Success",
                                  "description": "Indicates if the individual subrequest succeeded."
                                }
                              },
                              "description": "Response body from a single subrequest."
                            },
                            {
                              "type": "object",
                              "additionalProperties": {
                                "anyOf": [
                                  {
                                    "type": "string"
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "integer"
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "number"
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "boolean"
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "array",
                                    "items": {}
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "object",
                                    "additionalProperties": true
                                  },
                                  {
                                    "type": "null"
                                  }
                                ]
                              }
                            }
                          ],
                          "title": "Body",
                          "description": "The actual response data from the subrequest. For POST operations, contains id, success, and errors. For GET operations, contains the queried record data."
                        },
                        "httpHeaders": {
                          "type": "object",
                          "title": "Http Headers",
                          "description": "HTTP headers from the subrequest response (e.g., Location header for created resources).",
                          "additionalProperties": {
                            "type": "string"
                          }
                        },
                        "referenceId": {
                          "type": "string",
                          "title": "Reference Id",
                          "description": "The reference ID from the original request, used to match responses to requests."
                        },
                        "httpStatusCode": {
                          "type": "integer",
                          "title": "Http Status Code",
                          "description": "HTTP status code for the individual subrequest. Examples: 200 (OK), 201 (Created), 400 (Bad Request), 404 (Not Found)."
                        }
                      },
                      "description": "Response for a single subrequest within a composite graph."
                    },
                    "title": "Composite Response",
                    "description": "Array containing individual results for each subrequest in the graph."
                  }
                },
                "description": "Contains the execution results for the graph."
              }
            },
            "description": "Results for a single graph in the composite graph operation."
          },
          "title": "Graphs",
          "description": "Array containing results for each graph submitted. Each graph result includes the graphId, execution results for all subrequests, and overall success status."
        }
      },
      "description": "Data from the action execution"
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Error",
      "description": "Error if any occurred during the execution of the action"
    },
    "successful": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Successful",
      "description": "Whether or not the action execution was successful or not"
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_POST_COMPOSITE_SOBJECTS
Tool to create up to 200 records in one request using sObject Collections. Use when you need to create multiple records of potentially different sObject types efficiently in a single API call.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PostCompositeSobjectsRequest",
  "required": [
    "records"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "records": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "SObjectRecord",
        "required": [
          "attributes"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "attributes": {
            "type": "object",
            "title": "Attributes",
            "required": [
              "type"
            ],
            "properties": {
              "type": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Type",
                "examples": [
                  "Account",
                  "Contact",
                  "Lead",
                  "Opportunity",
                  "CustomObject__c"
                ],
                "description": "The sObject API name (e.g., 'Account', 'Contact', 'Lead', 'CustomObject__c'). Required for each record to identify which object type to create."
              }
            },
            "description": "Metadata identifying the sObject type for this record. Must include the 'type' field with the sObject API name.",
            "additionalProperties": false
          }
        },
        "description": "A single sObject record to create with its attributes and field values.",
        "additionalProperties": true
      },
      "title": "Records",
      "examples": [
        [
          {
            "Name": "Composite Test Account 1",
            "attributes": {
              "type": "Account"
            },
            "BillingCity": "San Francisco"
          },
          {
            "Name": "Composite Test Account 2",
            "attributes": {
              "type": "Account"
            },
            "BillingCity": "New York"
          }
        ]
      ],
      "maxItems": 200,
      "minItems": 1,
      "description": "Array of sObject records to create. Minimum 1 record, maximum 200 records per request. Each record must include an 'attributes' object with the 'type' field specifying the sObject API name (e.g., Account, Contact), followed by field name-value pairs. Records are created in the order listed."
    },
    "all_or_none": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "All Or None",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        false,
        true
      ],
      "description": "Determines whether the request should be processed atomically. When true, all records must succeed or the entire request is rolled back. When false (default), partial success is allowed and each record is processed independently."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_POST_PARAMETERIZED_SEARCH
Tool to execute parameterized search across Salesforce objects with advanced filtering. Use when you need to search for records using specific search terms with fine-grained control over which objects to search, which fields to return, and additional filtering criteria.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PostParameterizedSearchRequest",
  "required": [
    "q"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "q": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Q",
      "examples": [
        "test",
        "John Smith",
        "Acme Corporation",
        "555-1234"
      ],
      "description": "The search string to search for across Salesforce objects. This is the primary search term used in the SOSL FIND clause.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "The text you want to search for across Salesforce records. Enter keywords, names, phone numbers, or any text to find matching records."
    },
    "in": {
      "enum": [
        "ALL",
        "NAME",
        "EMAIL",
        "PHONE",
        "SIDEBAR"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "In",
      "examples": [
        "ALL",
        "NAME",
        "EMAIL",
        "PHONE"
      ],
      "description": "Search scope specifying which fields to search. Valid values: 'ALL' (ALL FIELDS), 'NAME' (NAME FIELDS), 'EMAIL' (EMAIL FIELDS), 'PHONE' (PHONE FIELDS), 'SIDEBAR' (SIDEBAR FIELDS). Defaults to 'ALL'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Scope",
      "human_parameter_description": "Limit the search to specific field types. For example, choose 'EMAIL' to only search email fields, or 'NAME' to only search name fields."
    },
    "where": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Where",
      "examples": [
        "CreatedDate > 2024-01-01",
        "IsActive = true"
      ],
      "description": "Global WHERE clause applied to all sObjects (without the WHERE keyword). Uses standard SOQL WHERE clause syntax.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Global Filter",
      "human_parameter_description": "A filter condition that applies to all object types being searched. Use SOQL WHERE clause syntax without the WHERE keyword."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Id",
          "Name"
        ],
        [
          "Id",
          "Name",
          "Email",
          "Phone"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Default fields to return for all sObjects if not specified per object. Field API names like ['Id', 'Name', 'Email'].",
      "human_parameter_name": "Default Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "Default list of fields to return for all objects (unless overridden for a specific object). Use field API names."
    },
    "sobjects": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "SObjectSpec",
        "required": [
          "name"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "name": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Name",
            "examples": [
              "Account",
              "Contact",
              "Lead",
              "Opportunity"
            ],
            "description": "The sObject API name to search (e.g., 'Contact', 'Account', 'Lead')."
          },
          "limit": {
            "type": "integer",
            "title": "Limit",
            "maximum": 2000,
            "minimum": 1,
            "description": "Maximum records to return for this object. If not specified, uses defaultLimit."
          },
          "where": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Where",
            "examples": [
              "CreatedDate > 2024-01-01",
              "Status = 'Active' AND Type = 'Customer'"
            ],
            "description": "WHERE clause filter for this specific object (without the WHERE keyword). Uses standard SOQL WHERE clause syntax."
          },
          "fields": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "title": "Fields",
            "examples": [
              [
                "Id",
                "Name",
                "Email"
              ],
              [
                "Id",
                "Name",
                "Phone",
                "Title"
              ]
            ],
            "description": "Field names to return for this object. If not specified, uses the default fields parameter."
          }
        },
        "description": "Specification for an sObject to search within."
      },
      "title": "Sobjects",
      "examples": [
        [
          {
            "name": "Account"
          }
        ],
        [
          {
            "name": "Contact",
            "limit": 10,
            "fields": [
              "Id",
              "Name",
              "Email"
            ]
          }
        ],
        [
          {
            "name": "Account",
            "where": "Industry = 'Technology'"
          },
          {
            "name": "Contact",
            "where": "Email != null"
          }
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Array of sObject specifications to limit search scope. Each object specifies which Salesforce object type to search and optional filters.",
      "human_parameter_name": "SObjects to Search",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify which Salesforce object types to search (like Account, Contact, Lead). You can also specify which fields to return and filters for each object."
    },
    "defaultLimit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Default Limit",
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Default limit per sObject when not specified in the sobjects array. Default is 25.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Default Limit per Object",
      "human_parameter_description": "The default maximum number of records to return for each object type (unless overridden for a specific object)."
    },
    "overallLimit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Overall Limit",
      "maximum": 2000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Maximum total number of records to return across all sObjects. Default is 2000, maximum is 2000.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Overall Limit",
      "human_parameter_description": "The maximum total number of records to return across all object types. Useful for limiting large result sets."
    },
    "spellCorrection": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Spell Correction",
      "description": "Enable spell correction for search terms. Default is true.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spell Correction",
      "human_parameter_description": "Whether to automatically correct spelling mistakes in the search query. Helps find results even with typos."
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_QUERY_ALL
Tool to execute SOQL queries including soft-deleted and archived records. Use when you need to query records that have been deleted via merge or delete operations, or when accessing archived Task and Event records.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "QueryAllRequest",
  "required": [
    "query"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE IsDeleted = true",
        "SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact",
        "SELECT Id, Subject, Status FROM Task WHERE IsArchived = true",
        "SELECT Id, Name, Amount FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10"
      ],
      "minLength": 10,
      "description": "The SOQL query to execute. Unlike standard queries, QueryAll includes soft-deleted records (from merge or delete operations) and archived Task/Event records. Example: 'SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE IsDeleted = true'. Use standard SOQL syntax.",
      "human_parameter_name": "SOQL Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "The SOQL query to execute. QueryAll returns deleted records and archived Task/Event records that standard queries exclude."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for QueryAll action"
}
```

```json
                "description": "ID of the User who last modified the contact record."
              },
              "LastModifiedDate": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Last Modified Date",

              },
              "MailingLongitude": {

                "description": "Longitude coordinate of the contact's mailing address."
              },
              "MailingPostalCode": {

                "description": "Postal or ZIP code component of the contact's mailing address."
              }
            },
            "description": "A single Contact record returned by the query."
          },
          "title": "Records",
          "description": "Array containing the Contact records returned by the query."
        },
        "totalSize": {
          "type": "integer",
          "title": "Total Size",
          "description": "The total number of records that can be selected with the SOQL query."
        },
        "nextRecordsUrl": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Next Records Url",
          "description": "Contains a query locator URL to retrieve the next batch of records. Only present when done is false and more than 2000 records match the query."
        }
      },
      "description": "Data from the action execution"
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Error",
      "description": "Error if any occurred during the execution of the action"
    },
    "successful": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Successful",
      "description": "Whether or not the action execution was successful or not"
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_QUERY_REPORT
DEPRECATED: Executes a Salesforce report synchronously by its `id` and `reportType`, optionally with dynamic ad-hoc adjustments like filters or groupings, and returns its data without modifying the saved report.

## SALESFORCE_REMOVE_ACCOUNT_BY_UNIQUE_IDENTIFIER
DEPRECATED: Deletes an existing Salesforce Account using its unique ID, returning an empty response on success (HTTP 204).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RemoveAccountByUniqueIdentifierRequest",
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Id",
      "examples": [
        "001R0000005hDFYIA2",
        "0012F00002h5G8VQ"
      ],
      "description": "Unique Salesforce Account ID (typically 15 or 18 characters).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Account ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique Salesforce Account ID of the account you want to delete. Use the 15- or 18-character ID from the account\u2019s URL to ensure the correct record is removed."
    }
  },
  "description": "Input to remove a Salesforce Account by its unique identifier."
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "RemoveAccountByUniqueIdentifierResponse": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "RemoveAccountByUniqueIdentifierResponse",
      "properties": {},
      "description": "Response schema for deleting a Salesforce Account.\n\nOn success (HTTP 204 No Content), the response body is empty - no fields are returned.\nOn error (4xx/5xx), Salesforce returns an array of error objects with 'message',\n'errorCode', and optional 'fields' array, but those are handled by HTTP error\nhandling before reaching this schema."
    }
  },
  "title": "RemoveAccountByUniqueIdentifierResponseWrapper",
  "required": [
    "data",
    "successful"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Data",
      "properties": {},
      "description": "Data from the action execution"
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Error",
      "description": "Error if any occurred during the execution of the action"
    },
    "successful": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Successful",
      "description": "Whether or not the action execution was successful or not"
    }
  }
}
```

## SALESFORCE_RETRIEVE_LEAD_BY_ID
Retrieves details for a Salesforce Lead by its ID; the specified Lead ID must exist in Salesforce.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RetrieveLeadByIdRequest",
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],

    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Id",
      "examples": [
        "00Q8c000001g3fHIEAY",
        "00Q5j000009k1XZEAY"
      ],

      "human_parameter_name": "Lead ID",

    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "examples": [
        "Name,Email,Status,Company",
        "FirstName,LastName,AnnualRevenue,Custom_Field__c"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-delimited list of Salesforce Lead field API names to return (e.g., Name,Email,Company). Field names must be exact API names (alphanumeric with underscores, no spaces). Custom fields typically end with '__c'. If omitted, all accessible fields are returned.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Field List",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the exact Salesforce field API names you want to retrieve, separated by commas. Field names must not contain spaces (e.g., 'Name,Email,Company' or 'FirstName,Custom_Field__c'). Use API names like 'MobilePhone' not descriptive text like 'Mobile Phone'. Leave blank to return all available fields."
    },
    "filtered_fields_message": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filtered Fields Message",
      "description": "Internal field to store message about filtered fields."
    }
  },
  "description": "Defines the request parameters for retrieving a Salesforce Lead by its ID."
}
```

## SALESFORCE_RETRIEVE_OPPORTUNITY_BY_ID_WITH_OPTIONAL_FIELDS
DEPRECATED: Retrieves a Salesforce Opportunity by its ID; the Opportunity ID must exist.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RetrieveOpportunityByIdWithOptionalFieldsRequest",
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Id",
      "examples": [
        "001R0000005hDFYIA2",
        "006aj000002QyDSAAS"
      ],
      "description": "The unique Salesforce ID of the Opportunity record to retrieve. This is a required path parameter.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Opportunity ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The Salesforce ID of the opportunity you want to look up. Copy it from the opportunity's URL or record details to fetch that specific opportunity."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "examples": [
        "Name,Amount,StageName,CloseDate",
        "Description,Type,LeadSource,NextStep"
      ],
      "description": "An optional, comma-delimited list of API names of the Opportunity fields to retrieve. If not specified, all accessible fields for the Opportunity object will be returned. This parameter is used as a query parameter in the GET request.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "Optional: list the opportunity fields you want returned, separated by commas (for example, Name,Amount,StageName). Leave blank to return all available fields."
    }
  },
  "description": "Defines the request parameters for retrieving a Salesforce Opportunity by its ID, with an option to specify desired fields."
}
```

## SALESFORCE_RETRIEVE_SPECIFIC_CAMPAIGN_OBJECT_DETAILS
DEPRECATED: Retrieves details for a specific Salesforce Campaign object by its ID, optionally limiting to specified fields; the Campaign object must exist.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RetrieveSpecificCampaignObjectDetailsRequest",
  "required": [
    "id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Id",
      "examples": [
        "001R0000005hDFYIA2"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier (ID) of the Salesforce Campaign object to retrieve. Example: '001R0000005hDFYIA2'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Campaign ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique Salesforce ID of the campaign you want to view. You can copy it from the campaign's URL in Salesforce or use an ID returned from a previous search."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "examples": [
        "name,description",
        "name,description,numberofemployees,industry"
      ],
      "description": "Optional comma-delimited list of field API names for the Campaign object whose values you want to retrieve (e.g., 'name,description,numberofemployees,industry'). Field names are case-sensitive and should match Salesforce API names. If unspecified, all accessible fields are returned.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "Which campaign details you want to return. Enter a comma-separated list like 'name,description'; leave blank to include all available fields."
    }
  },
  "description": "Defines the request parameters for the action to retrieve specific details of a Salesforce Campaign object."
}
```

## SALESFORCE_RUN_REPORT
Runs a report and returns the results. Creates a report instance that can be checked for completion. Results are returned in a nested structure (factMap, reportExtendedMetadata), not a flat record list; an empty factMap/rows is a valid result. Avoid repeated calls when freshness allows — reuse an existing instance_id instead.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RunReportRequest",
  "required": [
    "report_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "report_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Report Id",
      "examples": [
        "00OWd000001GtZ9MAK",
        "00OXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
      ],
      "description": "The Salesforce ID of the report to run.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Report ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The Salesforce ID of the report you want to run. You can copy it from the report's URL (it usually starts with 00O)."
    }
  }
}
```

```json
        },

          "type": "object",
          "title": "Fact Map",
          "description": "Contains values for summary or both summary and detailed data, expressed as keys which can be programmatically used to visualize the report data. Keys use patterns like 'T!T' for tabular reports, '0!T', '1!T' for row grouping totals, or '<rowGrouping>!<columnGrouping>' for matrix reports.",
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "object",
            "title": "FactMapValue",

              "rows": {
                "type": "array",

                  "type": "object",

                        "type": "object",

                          "label": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "title": "Label",
                            "description": "Human-readable formatted representation of the cell value."
                          },
                          "value": {
                            "title": "Value",
                            "description": "Machine-parseable value. Type varies by field type: string for text/picklist, number for numeric/percentage, object with 'amount' and 'currency' properties for currency, ISO date string for dates, Salesforce ID for reference fields, or null for empty fields."
                          },
                          "escapedLabel": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "title": "Escaped Label",
                            "description": "HTML-escaped version of the label."
                          }
                        },
                        "description": "Data cell containing a single cell value in a report row."
                      },
                      "title": "Data Cells",
                      "description": "Array of data cells containing the values for each column in the row."
                    }
                  },
                  "description": "Detail row containing data cells."
                },
                "title": "Rows",
                "description": "Array of detail rows, each containing dataCells with the actual report data."
              },
              "aggregates": {
                "type": "array",
                "items": {
                  "type": "object",

                  },
                  "description": "Aggregate value with label and numeric value."
                },
                "title": "Aggregates",
                "description": "Array of aggregate values with label and value pairs, such as totals, counts, or averages."
```

## SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY
Executes a SOQL query against Salesforce data. Returns records matching the query with pagination support.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ExecuteSoqlQueryRequest",
  "required": [
    "query"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact WHERE CreatedDate > 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account",
        "SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE Status = 'New'",
        "SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10",
        "SELECT FIELDS(ALL) FROM Account LIMIT 200",
        "SELECT Id, Name FROM Contact WHERE LastName = 'O\\'Brien'"
      ],
      "description": "Must be a valid SOQL statement starting with SELECT. Do NOT pass natural language descriptions of what data you need. SOQL query to execute. Use standard SOQL syntax. IMPORTANT ALIAS SYNTAX: SOQL does NOT support the 'AS' keyword for aliases (unlike SQL). Use implicit aliases without 'AS': 'SUM(Amount) TotalSales' NOT 'SUM(Amount) AS TotalSales'. If 'AS' keyword is detected, it will be automatically removed. IMPORTANT AGGREGATE QUERY RULES: When using aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX) without a GROUP BY clause: ORDER BY and LIMIT are NOT allowed at all (aggregate queries without GROUP BY return a single row, so ordering/limiting is meaningless). Invalid ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses will be automatically removed. To use ORDER BY/LIMIT with aggregates, add a GROUP BY clause. IMPORTANT: When using FIELDS(ALL) or FIELDS(CUSTOM) in the SELECT clause, a LIMIT clause is required with a maximum value of 200 (unbounded queries). FIELDS(STANDARD) does NOT require a LIMIT as it returns a bounded set of fields. If no LIMIT is provided or LIMIT exceeds 200 for unbounded queries, LIMIT 200 will be automatically added. Ensure ID values in WHERE clauses are wrapped in single quotes (e.g., AccountId = '0013W00000DaQ3lQAF'). For string literals containing apostrophes, use backslash escaping (e.g., Name = 'O\\'Brien' or Name LIKE '%D\\'AVEIA%'). SQL-style doubled single quotes (e.g., 'O''Brien') will be automatically converted to backslash escaping.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "The SOQL statement to run against your Salesforce data. Write the query that selects and filters the records you want to retrieve."
    }
  }
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "QueryRecord": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "QueryRecord",
      "required": [
        "attributes"
      ],
      "properties": {

          "type": "object",
          "title": "Attributes",
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "properties": {
            "url": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Url",
              "description": "The REST API endpoint URL to directly access this specific record. Not present for aggregate query results."
            },

              "type": "string",

              "description": "The Salesforce object type of this record (e.g., Account, Contact, Opportunity, AggregateResult)."
```

## SALESFORCE_SEARCH
DEPRECATED: Use SALESFORCE_EXECUTE_SOSL_SEARCH instead. Executes a SOSL search query across multiple Salesforce objects. Use when you need to search for text across multiple object types simultaneously.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchRequest",
  "required": [
    "q"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "q": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Q",
      "examples": [
        "FIND {test} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name)",
        "FIND {Acme} IN NAME FIELDS RETURNING Account(Name, Phone)",
        "FIND {john} RETURNING Contact(FirstName, LastName, Email)",
        "FIND {tech*} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Name), Lead(Name, Company) LIMIT 10"
      ],
      "description": "URL-encoded SOSL search query string to execute. Must follow SOSL syntax with FIND clause. Example: 'FIND {Acme} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Name, Phone), Contact(FirstName, LastName)'",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "The SOSL search query to execute. Use FIND clause to specify search terms (enclosed in curly braces) and RETURNING clause to specify objects and fields to retrieve."
    }
  }
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "SearchRecord": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "SearchRecord",
```

## SALESFORCE_SEARCH_ACCOUNTS
Search for Salesforce accounts using criteria like name, industry, type, location, or contact information. Always provide at least one filter parameter; omitting all filters returns a broad, slow listing. Owner/territory filtering is unsupported — use SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY for ownership-based filters. Use SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT to fetch complete field data for a specific record. Unsupported filter fields may be silently ignored — verify results reflect intended criteria.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchAccountsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "examples": [
        "Acme Corp",
        "Tech Solutions",
        "Inc"
      ],
      "description": "Search by account name. Supports partial matches.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Account Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "The account name you want to look up. Enter a full or partial name to find matching accounts."
    },
    "type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Type",
      "examples": [
        "Customer - Direct",
        "Customer - Channel",
        "Prospect",
        "Partner"
      ],
      "description": "Search by account type.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Account Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "The kind of relationship this account has with you (e.g., Customer, Prospect, Partner). Choose to filter results by type."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "default": 50,
      "maximum": 2000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Maximum number of accounts to return. Results are hard-capped at approximately 2000 rows; use more selective filters if the full dataset exceeds this.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Limit",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many accounts to return at most. Lower this to get a smaller, faster result set."
    },
    "phone": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Phone",
      "examples": [
        "555-1234",
        "800",
        "+1"
      ],
      "description": "Search by phone number. Supports partial matches. Requires field-level security access to the Phone field.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Phone Number",
      "human_parameter_description": "The account's phone number or part of it. Use this to find accounts by their phone number."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "default": "Id,Name,Type,Industry,Phone,Website,BillingStreet,BillingCity,BillingState,BillingCountry,NumberOfEmployees,AnnualRevenue",
      "examples": [
        "Id,Name,Type,Industry,Phone,Website",
        "Id,Name,Type,Industry,Phone,Website,BillingCity,BillingState,NumberOfEmployees"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of valid Salesforce Account field API names to retrieve. Only use actual field names like Id, Name, Industry, etc. Do not include type annotations or placeholders like <string> or <DATE_TIME>. If any field in this list is restricted by field-level security, the entire request will fail \u2014 use a minimal set of standard fields (e.g., Id,Name,Website) when access is uncertain.",
      "human_parameter_description": "Which account details you want back. Provide a comma-separated list of fields to include in the results."
    },
    "website": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Website",
      "examples": [
        "acme.com",
        ".com",
        "https://"
      ],
      "description": "Search by website. Supports partial matches.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Website",
      "human_parameter_description": "The account\u2019s website or part of it (like the domain). Use this to find accounts by their web address."
    },
    "industry": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Industry",
      "examples": [

        "Healthcare",
        "Manufacturing",
        "Financial Services"
      ],
      "description": "Search by industry.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Industry",
      "human_parameter_description": "The industry the account belongs to. Use a keyword to narrow results to accounts in that industry."
    },
    "billing_city": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Billing City",
      "examples": [

        "New York",
        "Chicago"
      ],
      "description": "Search by billing city. Supports partial matches.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Billing City",
      "human_parameter_description": "The city listed on the account\u2019s billing address. Enter a city name to filter matching accounts."
    },
    "billing_state": {
```

## SALESFORCE_SEARCH_CAMPAIGNS
Search for Salesforce campaigns using multiple criteria like name, type, status, date range, or active status. Requires access to the Campaign object (Marketing User feature must be enabled in the org). For complex sorting (multi-field ORDER BY), use SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY instead.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchCampaignsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "examples": [
        "Summer Sale",
        "Product Launch",
        "Webinar"
      ],
      "description": "Search by campaign name. Supports partial matches. Combine with type, status, or date range filters to narrow results when names are non-unique.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Campaign Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter part or all of the campaign name to find matching campaigns."
    },
    "type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Type",
      "examples": [
        "Email",
        "Webinar",
        "Trade Show",
        "Public Relations"
      ],
      "description": "Search by campaign type.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Campaign Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose the type of campaign to filter by, such as Email, Webinar, or Trade Show."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "default": 50,
      "maximum": 2000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Maximum number of campaigns to return. Check totalSize in the response to determine if results are truncated; issue additional queries if needed.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Limit",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set the maximum number of campaigns to return. Higher values show more results but may take longer."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "default": "Id,Name,Type,Status,StartDate,EndDate,IsActive,Description,BudgetedCost,ActualCost,NumberOfContacts,NumberOfLeads",
      "examples": [
        "Id,Name,Type,Status,StartDate,EndDate",
        "Id,Name,Type,Status,StartDate,EndDate,IsActive,BudgetedCost,ActualCost"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of Campaign fields to retrieve.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Fields",
      "human_parameter_description": "List the campaign details you want returned, separated by commas (for example: Id,Name,Status)."
    },
    "status": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Status",
      "examples": [
        "Planned",
        "In Progress",
        "Completed",
        "Aborted"
      ],
      "description": "Search by campaign status.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Campaign Status",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select the campaign status you want to see, like Planned, In Progress, Completed, or Aborted."
    },
    "is_active": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Is Active",
      "description": "Filter by active status. True for active campaigns, False for inactive.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Active Status",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose whether to include only active campaigns, only inactive ones, or leave blank to include both."
    },
    "start_date_to": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Date To",
      "examples": [
        "2024-12-31"
      ],
      "description": "Upper bound for StartDate (inclusive). Use YYYY-MM-DD.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Start Date To",
      "human_parameter_description": "Show campaigns that start on or before this date. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD."
    },
    "start_date_from": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Date From",
      "examples": [
        "2024-01-01"
      ],
      "description": "Lower bound for StartDate (inclusive). Use YYYY-MM-DD.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Start Date From",
      "human_parameter_description": "Show campaigns that start on or after this date. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD."
    }
  }
}
```
